Thanks Alex — looping in EngOps and SRE. Initial ask: can we get a timeline and short mitigation within 30m. From the quick metrics I pulled:
- Burst of large requests starting 09:04 caused simultaneous prefetches to target overlapping key ranges.
- KV eviction rate spiked; hot-shard backpressure caused batch lane starvation and retries.
- P95/P99 token latency doubled.

Immediate mitigation proposal (short window):
1) Reduce batching window from 25ms -> 8ms for the affected pool.
2) Disable speculative prefetching on the tenant for 30m.
3) Temporarily route 15% of traffic to cold path (no KV) to relieve hot partitions.

Please confirm who will own each step. Jonas — want exec visibility. Ben — please coordinate customer comms/credits.

I'll pull the runbook and perf dashboards; attaching a short checklist.

Subject: Re: High error rate / 504s on production - investigating

Summary of quick triage (ops):
- Root cause signal: a config rollout last night increased prefetch concurrency and changed key-range hashing for the multi-tenant KV layer. That increased overlap in prefetched keysets for some tenants (including StellarAI).
- Symptom: frequent concurrent writes to adjacent key groups triggered eviction churn; batching lanes blocked waiting on KV reads leading to HOL (head-of-line) blocking and cascading retries.

Actions taken now:
- Dialed prefetch concurrency for StellarAI down to baseline (from 8 -> 2).
- Reduced batch window for the affected pool to 10ms.
- Flushed a small set of stale hot-key entries (see heapdump note).

Preliminary effect (10:04): error-rate fell from 18% -> 6%; P99 token latency trending down but still ~2x normal.

Next recommended steps (30–90m):
- Revert the hashing change for the tenant’s shard allocation (will require a short maintenance window).
- Tuned KV TTL and aggressive LRU to reduce eviction churn.
- Run a controlled canary with throttled prefetch to validate.

I'm monitoring dashboards; will post updates every 20 minutes.

--
Grace O'Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
